He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange]] and was drafted by the [[NBA]]'s [[New York Knicks]] in 2010, with the eighth pick of the second round (38th overall). He was born in [[Syracuse, New York]], in the United States, but is also a Canadian citizen and has played for the [[Canada men's national basketball team|Canadian national team]]. He is the son of [[Leo Rautins]], who also played for Syracuse and professionally, and is the former coach of the Canadian national team. ==High school career== Rautins played on the 2004 [[Jamesville-Dewitt High School]] Class A state championship squad that went undefeated (29–0) after defeating [[St. Joseph's Collegiate Institute]], 77–73 (OT) in the championship game. Rautins led the way with 19 points and seven rebounds. He was named first-team all-state and first-team All-CNY.{{Cite web |url=http://www.suathletics.com/roster.asp?playerid=1968&sport=176&roster=194&path=mbasket |title=SUathletics.com – The Official Website of Syracuse University Athletics |access-date=2007-04-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070218213222/http://www.suathletics.com/roster.asp?playerid=1968&sport=176&roster=194&path=mbasket |archive-date=2007-02-18 |url-status=dead }} ==College career== [[File:AndyRautins.JPG|thumb|150px|left|Rautins during warmups before a game at [[Syracuse University]]'s [[Carrier Dome]] with Assistant Coach and former Syracuse Orange Basketball player [[Gerry McNamara]] watching.]] Rautins had offers from [[Providence College|Providence]] and [[St. Bonaventure University|St. Bonaventure]] before deciding on Syracuse.[http://interact.cstv.com/recruiting/column_archive_display.cfm?hodge_id=1492 CSTV.com: #1 in College Sports] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110708212017/http://interact.cstv.com/recruiting/column_archive_display.cfm?hodge_id=1492 |date=2011-07-08 }} At Syracuse, he majored in communication and rhetorical studies.{{cite web |url=http://suathletics.syr.edu/roster.aspx?rp_id=6926&path=mbasket |title=Syracuse University Athletics – 2009–10 Men's Basketball Roster |publisher=Suathletics.syr.edu |access-date=2012-01-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100430154558/http://suathletics.syr.edu/roster.aspx?rp_id=6926&path=mbasket |archive-date=2010-04-30 |url-status=dead }} ===2005–06=== Rautins was used sparingly his freshman year, appearing in just 20 games. He averaged 2.9 points and 0.9 rebounds, but did set a then-career high of 10 points against South Florida on January 8, 2006, connecting on 3-of-5 3-point attempts.{{citation needed|date=January 2012}} ===2006–07=== In his sophomore season, Rautins appeared in all 35 of Syracuse's games, including his first career start against Baylor on December 16, 2006. Rautins remained a fixture in the Syracuse starting lineup, and set a career high with 19 points against Providence on February 24, 2007. He finished the season averaging 7.2 points. Rautins established himself as one of the team's best perimeter shooters, converting 36 percent of his 3-point shots. ===2007–08=== Rautins missed the entire season because of a knee injury suffered during the Tournament of the Americas in Las Vegas over the 2007 summer. He was granted a medical [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]]. ===2008–09=== Rautins would return for his redshirt junior year after reconstructive surgery on his knee. His return paid immediate dividends for the Orange, as Rautins tied a school record with nine 3-pointers (Gerry McNamara had nine against BYU in the NCAA tournament in 2004) highlighting a career-high 29 points in an 82–71 victory over [[Coppin State]] on December 22, 2008.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=283570183 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231103224247/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=283570183 |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 3, 2023 |title=Coppin State Eagles vs. Syracuse Orange – Recap – December 22, 2008 – ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=2008-12-22 |access-date=2012-01-23}} Rautins would continue his tear against Seton Hall (26 points on 7–10 shooting from three point land), South Florida (14, 4–8) and DePaul (17, 5–10). In those four games, Rautins would hit a combined 25 3-pointers at a 57 percent clip.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4285/andy-rautins |title=Andy Rautins Stats, Bio – ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=2012-01-23}} Other highlights included Rautins 20 points, and six 3-pointers in the epic six overtime game against Connecticut in the Big East tournament. Rautins played 50 minutes off the bench and made a crucial 3-pointer in the final seconds of the third overtime, forcing a fourth. Rautins also made the go-ahead 3-pointer in the sixth overtime, giving Syracuse their first lead since the end of regulation to help lead to the historic win.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=290710041 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171213011206/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=290710041 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 13, 2017 |title=Syracuse Orange vs. Connecticut Huskies – Recap – March 12, 2009 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=2009-03-12 |access-date=2012-01-23}} ===2009–10=== Rautins would become the full-time starter at shooting guard in his senior season. On November 20, 2009, Rautins would lead Syracuse to an 87–71 upset of then-No. 4 North Carolina with 11 points, seven rebounds, seven assists and seven steals.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=293240153 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210303093050/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=293240153 December 10, 2009, Rautins played 39 minutes and scored 16 points and handed out five assists as Syracuse knocked off then-No. 10 Florida 85–73.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=293440057 |title=Syracuse Orange vs. Florida Gators – Box Score – December 10, 2009 – ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=2009-12-10 web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=300140164 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210305095309/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=300140164 He started the gold medal game against Australia and scored a Canadian team tournament high 20 points including draining five three-pointers in the first half of the game. Rautins also played in the 2005 FIBA World U21 Championship in Argentina. He averaged 9.4 points in five games. In the bronze medal game, Rautins scored 11 points.{{cite web|url=http://www.basketball.ca/en/hm/download.php?id=691 |title=Canada Basketball |publisher=Basketball.ca |access-date=2012-01-23 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111001225556/http://www.basketball.ca/en/hm/download.php?id=691 |archive-date=2011-10-01 }} In 2006, Rautins played for the Canadian senior men's national team. The squad played a 10-game exhibition schedule in Europe during July and August. In a game against Venezuela at the International Alpos Cup, Rautins scored seven points and recorded three steals in 19 minutes. He also played in one game against Germany recording three points in eight minutes. Rautins played in all three games of the Diego Gianatti Tournament averaging 10.3 minutes and 2.3 points, including five points against Greece. Rautins participated in the [[Basketball at the 2007 Pan American Games|2007 Pan American Games]] held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, averaging a squad-best 14.4 points and 2.4 assists. He scored 16 points in a preliminary loss to Brazil.http://carrierdome.syr.edu/News/basketball/mbasket/2007/7/30/RautinsPanAm7.30.07.asp?path=mbasket{{dead link|date=July 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} During the same summer, he also played for Team Canada in the Tournament of Americas held in Las Vegas and tore his ACL during Canada's loss to Brazil.[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=2988460&campaign=rss&source=NCBHeadlines ESPN – Syracuse guard Rautins hurt in Tournament of Americas – Men's College Basketball]
